## Natural history notes

A small, nonnative lizard characterized by its brown to grayish body, variable darker markings, and a bright orange to red throat fan in males. In Florida, it is common in disturbed and urban habitats such as yards, gardens, sidewalks, parks, roadsides, and building edges. It is active during the day and often seen basking on low vegetation, fences, walls, and tree trunks, feeding mainly on small insects and other invertebrates.
